heading: CHAPTER XXI.
title: HOW A PRINCE SHOULD CONDUCT HIMSELF SO AS TO GAIN RENOWN
exclusions: front matter and dedication before THE PRINCE
notes: Chapter 21 argues that princes gain renown through visible enterprises, memorable internal examples, decisive alliances, and public encouragement of civic activity.
The chapter opposes renown to neutrality. Safety-seeking indecision leaves a prince at the mercy of conquerors, while declared alignment creates debts, bonds, and clearer political shape.

The closing movement broadens renown beyond war: patronage of ability, protection of productive life, festivals, and selective sociability all matter, but the prince must never let courtesy dissolve majesty.
